title: Vanishing constant and linear coefficients imply membership in the quadratic variables ideal
statement: Let R be any commutative ring, sigma a finite set, T=R[[X_i : i in sigma]] [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], and N the ideal generated by the X_i. If f in T has zero constant coefficient and zero coefficient of X_i for every i, then f belongs to N^2. The empty set of variables and the zero coefficient ring are allowed.

source.place: Tag 07EI, construction of f_1; coefficient field from Algebra Tag 032A

proof.text: For a nonzero exponent E, choose i with e_i <= E. If E-e_i=0, E is a single unit exponent. Otherwise choose j with e_j <= E-e_i, obtaining e_i+e_j <= E. Thus an exponent without two variable factors is zero or a single unit exponent, and its coefficient in f is zero by hypothesis.

When sigma is empty, every exponent is zero and f=0. Otherwise choose for every exponent E with two variable factors one pair p(E)=(i,j) with e_i+e_j <= E. Define g_ij at exponent D to be coeff_(D+e_i+e_j)(f) when p(D+e_i+e_j)=(i,j), and zero otherwise. These are actual coefficientwise series; every choice is justified by the proved existence of the pair.

Using coeff_monomial_mul, compare coefficients of f and sum_(i,j) X_i X_j g_ij. At an exponent E with two factors, exactly its chosen pair contributes, and the subtraction and readdition of e_i+e_j recover E. At any other exponent every summand has coefficient zero, as does f. Therefore the series are equal.
Each X_i X_j belongs to N^2, hence so does X_i X_j g_ij. The set of pairs is finite, so the displayed finite sum belongs to N^2, proving the claim.

theorem mem_span_X_sq_of_coeff_eq_zero (σ : Type u) [Finite σ]
    (R : Type v) [CommRing R] (f : MvPowerSeries σ R)
    (h0 : constantCoeff f = 0)
    (h1 : ∀ i : σ, coeff (Finsupp.single i 1) f = 0) :
    f ∈ (Ideal.span (Set.range (fun i ↦ (X i : MvPowerSeries σ R)))) ^ 2
